title: Off-main Canvas and Semantic Legend Pattern for Accessible, Low-power Time-series
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Goal: Design a reusable pattern that (1) renders high-density time-series visuals off the main thread to reduce jank and battery usage on low-powered devices, and (2) exposes a compact, semantic legend and tooltip API that screen readers can consume without requiring DOM-heavy traces per series.

Context: Current time-series components render complex layers (lines, bandlines, annotations) on the main thread using SVG and DOM overlays for tooltips/legends. This leads to frame drops on low-end laptops and mobile, and a proliferation of DOM nodes makes semantic grouping for assistive tech brittle. We need a pattern that offloads heavy painting to an off-main-thread canvas worker (or use OffscreenCanvas where available), preserves pixel crispness for high-DPI, and provides an accessible, lightweight abstraction for legends and tooltips that is keyboard- and screen-reader-first.

Proposed solution overview:
- Rendering: adopt an off-main-thread canvas renderer with a fallback to a well-optimized onscreen canvas. Use a single retained bitmap per view port and incremental tile updates for panning/zooming. Provide a "reduced-paint" mode driven by tokens (motion, density) for battery-sensitive clients.
- Legend pattern: introduce a semantic legend component that lives in the DOM as a compact list of accessible controls (checkbox-like toggles), but lazy-loads detailed micro-interaction overlays only on demand. Legend items expose aria-label, aria-pressed, and data-describedby links to a lightweight status region for dynamic updates (counts, highlighted series).
- Tooltip pattern: tooltips are lightweight DOM summaries that receive detailed geometry from the renderer via a shallow message (series id, x, y, short text). The renderer does NOT create DOM per series; it posts hit-test results to the main thread. For screen readers, provide a keyboard-focused "inspector" mode that converts the tooltip snapshot into a detailed aria-live announcement and programmatic focus trap.
- Performance/accessibility trade-offs: prefer message-based hit-testing over DOM hit areas to reduce node count; ensure hit testing is deterministic for keyboard traversal. Implement a configurable debounce for live announcements to avoid excessive speech.

Acceptance criteria:
- Demo: interactive prototype with 10k points across 6 series that maintains 60fps on modern laptops and avoids major jank on mid-range phones (measured: main-thread idle > 12ms during continuous animation).
- Accessibility: keyboard-only users can traverse series via legend, invoke inspector mode that reads detailed series metrics via aria-live, and screen readers get meaningful summaries without reading tens of thousands of DOM nodes.
- Tokens: new tokens for reduced-paint-mode, canvas-tile-size, legend-compact-threshold documented in design tokens.
- Developer ergonomics: charting API exposes a simple config {renderer: 'offscreen'|'canvas', accessibilityMode: 'compact'|'detailed', reducedPaint: true|false}.

Non-goals: This ticket does not include migrating all existing chart instances or adding audit automation; it's a pattern and prototype with docs and integration guidance.
